rationale: Essential consumables with Census-level margin data (23.9% GM, ~6% op margin) but that is incumbent economics; newcomer lacks rebates/volume pricing. rationale: No pricing or demand evidence (single Census source); founder lacks trade estimating skill. rationale: Mandated semiannual inspections, reachable buyers, low capital; but standalone ceiling modest, restaurant churn/bad debt high, and manufacturer authorization (parts access) unverified and possibly the binding gate. Pricing is analyst estimate. Better as add-on to extinguisher route than standalone.

Dense Chicago logistics base and real cost-per-load wedge with equipment service, but commodity products vs Uline/consolidators, resin price swings, net-30-60 terms and bulky inventory. Incumbent ~6% op margin; newcomer lower. ROIC ~30-60% once scaled; customer concentration risk.
red_flags: Supplier pricing for new distributor unknown

rationale: Real need but Illinois-only, contested by entrenched lien software (Levelset/Procore) and law firms. Preparing lien claims for others risks unauthorized practice of law; attorney fee-splitting limits. Missed deadlines create heavy liability. No spend evidence; stated ceiling ~$10k/mo.

Mandated annual tests drive inbound demand, but founder cannot test (needs licensed plumber-CCCDI; plumber license needs 4-yr apprenticeship). Scarce, costly licensed labor on $75-200 tickets plus price competition from any plumber compress margins. Payroll precedes density. Pricing/volume are estimates.
red_flags: Margin viability depends on hiring scarce CCCDI plumbers
Plumbing contractor registration requirements on firm

rationale: Founder's lab background helps, but universities are locked into Fisher/VWR contracts and Chicago startup cluster is small and price-shops Amazon. Only incumbent (Avantor) economics cited; author's own yr3 range starts at $0. Slow university AP, private-label quality risk, biotech funding cycles.

Founder can build it cheaply, but the underlying data is free and public; willingness to pay is unproven and national lead databases exist. Stated ceiling ~$5k/mo; trivially copied; seasonal contractor churn. Better as an internal lead tool than a business.

Strong recurring, health-code-driven demand; Rollins commercial GM 52.8% and many small IL operators show a viable small-start model. Founder can certify in months; public CDPH pest-violation data gives a prospect list. Crowded with nationals/independents; tech quality and retention decide churn. Pricing is estimated; consolidator exit plausible.

Census 4.5% average commission and MANA illustration (owner keeps ~30%) support modest economics. Founder's technical background fits design-in selling, but 6-24 month design cycles mean long unpaid ramp, unproven agencies get weak lines, and lines get pulled once developed. Territory-capped; relationship-heavy so hard to delegate.
red_flags: Signing 5-8 viable lines in 12 months assumed

rationale: Low-barrier, seasonal (May-Oct) commodity trade with many small operators and price-shopping property managers. Census op margin is a broad 238990 proxy. Satellite-measured proposals help speed but are easily copied. Deferrable spend in downturns; snow adjacency helps utilization. Realistic FCF ~$60-120k.

No spending or market-size data at all; economics entirely analyst estimates. Lumpy project revenue with thin maintenance recurrence, work-at-height risk, niche ceiling. Moderate competition and low capital make it a reasonable add-on to commercial pest control rather than a standalone base.

Shrinking independent retail, small orders, and Faire-type marketplaces disintermediating reps. Commission rate (~15%) unverified; payment often 60-90+ days after retailer pays. Author's own range $0-70k and $10k/mo ceiling. Founder-relationship bound; discretionary demand.

But founder lacks trade skill, needs a supervising licensed mason, scarce W-2 masons, heavy fall/insurance risk, seasonality, crowded field. Deposits help cash.
